method: Read paragraphs 190–210 together; support the disclaimer and concrete initiation vocabulary without repairing uncertain source wording or treating hypothetical claims as facts.
phrases: pledged
committed to joining a fraternity as a prospective member
承诺加入兄弟会；成为待正式入会的新成员
He pledged a fraternity during his first year at college.
他在大学一年级时成为了一个兄弟会的待入会成员。
Campus-specific use of pledge, not donating money or completing full initiation. Membership procedures vary; this explains the narrator's wording only.
vague
not specific or clearly detailed
含糊的；不具体的
The schedule is still vague about the starting time.
日程对开始时间仍说得不够明确。
Here the narrator calls the overview nonspecific. Useful combinations: a vague description, vague about the details; vagueness is not proof of falsehood.
directed towards
aimed at or intended for a particular target
针对；面向
My feedback was directed towards the process, not the team.
我的反馈针对的是流程，而不是团队。
Not directed towards one organization denies a specific target. Towards is figurative here, not physical travel; directed at is also natural in the teaching context.
representative of
typical of or accurately reflecting a wider group
能代表……的；体现……普遍情况的
One complaint is not necessarily representative of all customers' views.
一条投诉不一定能代表所有顾客的看法。
Shouldn't be taken as representative of means should not be interpreted as typical of. Its object continues in paragraph 195; the negative scope must be retained.
got spanked
was hit on the buttocks, usually as punishment
被打屁股
In the novel, the character got spanked as a child.
小说中的这个人物小时候被打过屁股。

Get + past participle forms a conversational passive. Here this is a concrete action in the narrator's initiation account, not figurative defeat; the teaching example describes rather than endorses it.
raw onion
an onion that has not been cooked
生洋葱
Would you like raw onion in your salad?
你的沙拉里要加生洋葱吗？
Raw means uncooked, not necessarily unripe; entire adds the meaning of a whole onion. The source describes coercion, unlike the voluntary food example.
forced to plank
made to hold the body straight in a supported exercise position against one's will
被迫做平板支撑
In the story, the recruits were forced to plank as punishment.
故事里的新成员被迫做平板支撑作为惩罚。
Plank is an exercise verb here, not a wooden board. Forced to describes coercion; while being spanked and then forced compress passive actions affecting the same person.
professing your undying love
declaring that your love will never end
宣称自己永不改变的爱
You don't need to write a speech professing your undying love to thank someone for coffee.
感谢别人请你喝咖啡，不必写篇演说来宣告自己永恒的爱。
Profess means declare, not prove sincerity; undying is deliberately elevated or exaggerated. In the source the declaration is coerced and addressed to fraternity brothers, not literal siblings.
the pinnacle of
the highest point or most impressive example of something
……的顶峰；……的最高境界
She regarded the award as the pinnacle of her career.
她把这个奖项看作自己职业生涯的顶峰。

Usually praise, but here sarcastic after descriptions of coercion and a power trip. Do not present this as genuine praise of the relationships; paragraph 207 still has an unresolved transcription problem.
segments: Read through 195: a hypothetical member's experience is interrupted by a disclaimer, not asserted about every organization. Pledged, nonspecific scope, target and representative-of construction are explicitly taught; got hazed is passive and shouldn't be taken as means should not be interpreted as.

This fragment supplies the object of representative of in 194. Keep the preceding shouldn't: the speaker disclaims representing any specific organization or all organizations; the awkward wording is preserved, not converted into a universal allegation.

The concrete bodily action and get-passive are taught explicitly. Yes links back to the hypothetical member's initiation despite loss of membership; no new factual allegation or endorsement is introduced.

Support covers uncooked whole food, passive punishment, the exercise meaning of plank and exaggerated declaration. While marks simultaneous actions, then sequences coercion; the omitted you are continues before forced. Brothers refers to fraternity members, not relatives, and declaring love does not prove sincere affection.

Pinnacle and sarcastic praise now have explicit support: obviously can only mean is ironic after the coercive actions. The opening still attaches to the uncertain you're big in 207; retain the source ambiguity rather than approving the complete linked passage.
